findings.title: canManage() grants on VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin holding only an all-groups VIEW permission passes requireManage(). That lets a view-only admin create top-level groups via addTopLevelGroup. The check should accept only the MANAGE scope.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource id instead of group id
findings.body: In V2 the resource name is the group id, but the code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission and adds it to the result. hasPermission looks the resource up by name, so the id lookup fails and falls back to the all-groups resource. The returned set then holds authz resource ids rather than group ids, so user search and count filtering by group (UserModel.GROUPS) will not match the intended groups. Use groupResource.getName() in both places.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is unsupported or the realm was initialized before the Groups type existed. That null is passed straight to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(). Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change will not have a Groups resource, so every group permission check can throw.

findings.title: Permissions not filtered by resource id
findings.body: Unlike UserPermissionsV2, this loop does not check that permission.getResourceId() equals the evaluated resource's id. Permissions granted on other resources could therefore satisfy the scope check.
